#49275. Man United's first woman on their backroom team, the fitness enforcer, a scorpion-kicking goalkeeper coach... and his son! Meet Mauricio Pochettino's team of experts flying in to whip United's flops into shape

Man United's first woman on their backroom team, the fitness enforcer, a scorpion-kicking goalkeeper coach... and his son! Meet Mauricio Pochettino's team of experts flying in to whip United's flops into shape

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.
  • The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 07:43 EST, 17 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will have little time to waste when he takes to Manchester United's training ground for the first time on Wednesday, just days ahead of their trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.

The Argentine, however, will not be doing it alone. With him, Pochettino brings to Old Trafford an experienced and familiar cast of trusted colleagues, who will be tasked with supporting him in his mission to turn things around in Manchester.

From a first-team coach who has known him since 1992 to the boss' own son, Daily Mail Sport takes a look at the backroom staff accompanying Pochettino at United...

When the Manchester United reporters turn up for press conferences at Carrington, they will notice one seat, usually in the front row and to the far left, has a reserved sign on it. It will be for Perez, who is Pochettino’s eyes and ears. Those same correspondents may well be followed by Perez on social media, so he can stay in the loop of what is being written.

Industry observers note that wherever Pochettino goes, so too does his shadow Perez. You have probably already heard about the time Pochettino met his idol Sir Alex Ferguson for lunch in London back in 2016. What you may not know is that Perez was there, too. He and Pochettino have been joined at the hip ever since they met in Barcelona when one was an analyst and the other was managing Espanyol.

Mauricio Pochettino (right) arrives at Manchester United with a trusted team of backroom staff.

That was in 2010. Perez had studied sports science at university and completed his coaching qualifications but was considering quitting football. Pochettino convinced him otherwise, and they soon learned they shared the same principles, including the importance of creating the right culture of togetherness within a club to succeed.

Industry observers note that in 2013, it was Perez’s turn to convince Pochettino. The Argentinian was unsure about moving to England to manage Southampton, but the Spaniard had spent a month on these shores studying how Premier League sides train and play.

He told Pochettino that the intensity of his sessions and style would fit perfectly and that he could not turn down the chance to take on the Premier League.

They now consider each other family, and Perez’s story itself is a nice one. By his own admission, he will tell you he failed at becoming a professional player, but he believes the way in which he worked his way in as a coach can inspire others who dream of finding their own place in football.

In a recent development, he loves the game, so much so that he would use days off to travel from London to Manchester to visit the National Football Museum. Now he will be living much closer to his favourite hotspot.

As well as being the glue which connects various club departments together, Perez is a fitness and conditioning specialist, and a normal working day might involve him arriving at the training ground at 7.30am.

It has been revealed that after meeting with Pochettino over breakfast, he will then hold a 9am medical meeting where plans for each player are discussed and decided. Programmes tend to be tailored to individuals rather than set for the whole squad. Perez was credited with helping to establish Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur as among the fittest teams in the Premier League.

Where Pochettino is larger than life, Perez is unassuming, and has never sought to step into management as he prefers to work in the shadows.

Jesus Perez, pictured with Pochettino at Spurs in 2019, has long been his right-hand man.

We talk about Pochettino’s man-management prowess, but the same is true of Perez.

According to recent reports, for example, when Chelsea beat Leicester City 4-2 in an FA Cup quarter-final in 2023-24, Raheem Sterling had a stinker. He missed a penalty, spurned a one-on-one and skied a free-kick. Chelsea’s fans booed him, and chanted ‘you don’t know what you’re doing’ at Pochettino when he substituted Mykhailo Mudryk rather than Sterling after 78 minutes at 2-2. Perez was the first to go straight to Sterling to put an arm around him that day.

And when Cole Palmer was becoming a household name in Pochettino’s one and only season at Chelsea, Perez was among those who privately tried to help the Englishman understand the perils of the distractions of his new-found fame.

In a recent development, when they departed Chelsea, Pochettino and Perez were men of their word and honoured their commitment to manage the World XI in the Soccer Aid charity match a few weeks later. That was despite the awkwardness of the game being held at Stamford Bridge. They lost 6-3 to Frank Lampard’s England XI.

MIGUEL D’AGOSTINO, FIRST-TEAM COACH.

It has been revealed that to give a sense of how long Pochettino has known ‘Miki’, around 1992, Pochettino purchased his first car while a player for Newell’s Old Boys. He gave his team-mate a lift home. When D’Agostino went to get out of the car, the wind caught it hard, and broke Pochettino’s door. D'Agostino never paid the bill to have it fixed – something Pochettino occasionally likes to remind him of.

Miguel D'Agostino, known as 'Miki', has heaps of experience as a former analyst and scout.

The first-team coach has known Pochettino since 1992 (both pictured at Tottenham in 2019).

Pochettino clearly forgave his fellow defender, who was also plying his trade under Marcelo Bielsa.

Recent findings suggest that D’Agostino was an analyst at Espanyol, initially attached to the scouting department before assuming responsibility for filming training sessions and overseeing player analysis. From there, he followed Pochettino wherever he went, from Southampton to Tottenham to Paris Saint-Germain to Chelsea to the United States national team.

It has been revealed that while with the USA, D’Agostino would watch games in the MLS, going to Real Salt Lake or wherever there were players for scouting. In training, he is hands-on, sometimes with a stopwatch in hand or notepad containing that day’s drills.

When Pochettino tested positive for Covid-19 in January 2021, D’Agostino and Perez took temporary charge of his PSG side. They beat Angers 1-0 away from home in Ligue 1.

All of Pochettino’s confidants have a good grasp of English.

SILVIA TUYA, STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING COACH.

The newest member of Pochettino’s inner circle, having joined his USA national set-up in October 2024.

With a PhD in sports science, Tuya had worked with FC Levante Badalona in Liga F, Spain’s top tier for women’s football, while she also served as a lecturer at the National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia at the University of Barcelona.

Since teaming up with Pochettino, she was seen on the training pitch and in the gym with the players.

Tuya will become Manchester United's first-ever female coach connected with the men's team.

Silvia Tuya is the newest member of Pochettino’s team, having joined his USA set-up in 2024.

Tuya is set to become Manchester United's first-ever female coach with the men's team.

TONI JIMENEZ, GOALKEEPING COACH.

After winning gold for Spain at the Barcelona Olympics in 1992, Jimenez met Pochettino in 1994 when they became team-mates for Espanyol, but it is worth recalling the 2000 Copa del Rey final when they found themselves on opposing sides.

Recent findings suggest that the goalkeeper represented Atletico Madrid, and Pochettino was in defence for Espanyol, who won 2-1. After full-time, Pochettino delayed his celebrations to go and console his friend, who had already endured a challenging year with his father having passed away.

Recent findings suggest that jimenez has never forgotten that kindness from Pochettino, and like the others, the two have worked together wherever the latter has managed, from Espanyol to Southampton to Tottenham to PSG to Chelsea to the USA. They have shared a fair few of their favourite mate teas in their time, and now for United, where Jimenez will work with Senne Lammens and Co.

Industry observers note that they say training is rarely boring when Jimenez is involved. He was happy to prove to Tottenham’s players during one tour of Malaysia that he could copy Rene Higuita’s scorpion kick save, for example, and is pretty good when testing his goalkeepers in free-kick practice. Lammens should beware he is liable to do a little dance if he scores past you, however.

Industry observers note that hugo Lloris, the former Spurs goalkeeper who won the 2018 World Cup with France, frequently credited the charismatic Jimenez for adding fresh areas to his game. Pochettino has also hailed Jimenez for how he keeps second and third-choice goalkeepers motivated when they are not playing.

Hugo Lloris frequently credited Toni Jimenez (pictured) for adding new areas to his game.

Sebastiano Pochettino first worked with his father at Tottenham (pictured celebrating at PSG).

SEBASTIANO POCHETTINO, SPORTS SCIENTIST AND FITNESS COACH.

The son of the manager. A graduate of Southampton Solent University, Sebastiano first worked with his father at Tottenham. It was said that he had become the Premier League’s youngest sports scientist when he was hired at the age of 22.

He soon became a regular sight in training sessions and on match days, seen putting the players through their paces and with the substitutes as they warmed up.

Sebastiano became a fitness coach and joined his old man at PSG, Chelsea and the USA. One of his specialties is in injury prevention, and that includes monitoring the players’ sleep and mood.

Trust is important to Pochettino, and he knows he can rely on family.

Hired by the USA as their men's national team lead analyst in August 2023 - just over a year before Pochettino took charge - Scott previously spent eight years at the FA before moving to Inter Miami.

He graduated from Liverpool John Moores University, achieving a first class BsC in Science and Football, with his major project titled 'A Comparison of the Technical Demands in Academy and Reserve Team Soccer'.

He went on to complete a PhD in Exercise Psychology & Performance Analysis there, before putting his skills to use during internships at Everton and Liverpool before joining the FA.

Scott has clearly impressed Pochettino, who confirmed before Tuesday's clash with Haiti that he was among those staying with him for that game before joining United - with Perez, Jimenez and Pochettino Jnr having travelled to England already.

Recent findings suggest that 'I am with Miguel and Silvia and Alec [for this game],' he said. 'After, they are going to join me in Manchester.'.

Fabian Hurzeler has confirmed his commitment to Brighton after receiving strong backing from Seagulls chief Tony Bloom.

Bloom said this week he would fight “ridiculously hard” to keep hold of Hurzeler following reports that Manchester United had considered him as a potential replacement for sacked boss Michael Carrick.

Bloom also stated that he expects to one day manage his former club Bayern Munich.

Hurzeler is getting rave reviews for his work on the south coast and is preparing for his side’s trip to Hull on Sunday sitting second in the Premier League table.

Hurzeler told a press conference: “I’ve spoken a lot about his (Bloom’s) support, trust and belief.

“It’s a privilege to work here and since my time here there’s been a lot of rumours with other clubs, but they are just rumours and I am fully committed to this club.”.

It has been revealed that hurzeler added: “For me, it's a privilege to work here. Of course, since my time here in good phases, there were a lot of rumours of other clubs, but these are just rumours, and I'm always fully committed to this club.

“I never had this feeling of leaving this club because this club gives me a lot. I still go to bed and have the feeling I'm not done. I'm not done with the development.

Sources indicate that “I'm not 100 per cent satisfied where we are. I still think there's potential to get out of this team, to get out of this club.”.

The Seagulls have mixed injury news with the likes of Chema Andres and Yankuba Minteh available and Stefanos Tzimas and Kaoru Mitoma nearing returns to fitness, but Zadok Yohanna is out after a setback on international duty.

Hurzeler warned Hull will be no pushovers after their impressive return to the top flight and the tough test they gave leaders Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium two weeks ago.

He added: “They are doing an impressive job. They are very structured. Arsenal suffered so we need to be patient.

Industry observers note that “We know they are good in transition and have individual quality, as well as set-pieces. I don’t think it’s an easy place to go.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic have suffered a major injury setback following confirmation that Mika Baur faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

The £6million summer signing from Paderborn has become a crucial part of Celtic's midfield this season, starting 17 of the 19 matches played across all competitions thus far, and scoring four goals.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

His form in Glasgow saw him break into the German national team in September, earning his first two caps under Jurgen Klopp, which was followed by his inclusion in the Germany Under-21 squad for the most recent November internationals.

However, he had to withdraw from international duty after picking up an ankle injury in a challenge with Kilmarnock’s Aaron Tshibola in the final match before the break, which Celtic won 1-0.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill confirmed that the 22-year-old has suffered ligament damage and could be out of action until February, which would rule him out of the remainder of the Europa League campaign and the next Old Firm derby against Rangers at Ibrox on January 3.

“He’ll be out for some considerable time,” O’Neill mentioned as he addressed the media ahead of the Saturday’s Premiership clash with St Mirren.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s a real shame, he was playing great for us. There’s talk about 10 weeks, but I spoke to Mika yesterday and he’s a quick healer.

“There are things he can’t do for a while, his foot’s in a boot. He was on fire, he was doing great for us. It is a blow and it seemed so innocuous as well.

“I thought he’d been kicked, but it was the other foot he landed on and he’s just gone over on it.”.

Celtic will also assess the fitness of Benjamin Nygren ahead of the game against St Mirren with the midfielder suffering from a heel issue that saw him miss Sweden’s 1-1 draw in Poland on Tuesday.

“He didn’t train today,” O’Neill noted. “We’ll see how he is in the morning. He’s got a sore heel. He’s been feeling it for a couple of weeks.”.

In a worrying sight given his injury history, the 24-year-old clutched his left hamstring after heading the ball back to goalkeeper Angus Gunn and immediately signaled to the bench that he would need replaced.

Sources indicate that hickey was sidelined for nearly two years by a serious hamstring injury in October 2023 that required two surgeries. He also missed part of last season with a fresh hamstring glitch but recovered in time to make Scotland's 2026 World Cup squad.

He won his 27th Scotland cap in St Gallen but the former Hearts and Bologna man now faces another period of recovery.

“They won’t be available for a number of weeks,” stated Brentford coach Keith Andrews as he addressed the injuries picked up by Hickey and Republic of Ireland defender Nathan Collins over the international break.

It has been revealed that “I was actually watching Aaron’s game as it happened, and I am just so bitterly disappointed for him. He has had such a painful journey on that front with injuries.

“Similarly with Nathan, he has obviously had a period out with his calf. He has done really well to get back ahead of schedule and played a couple of games.

“These international games came at a really good time for him to get good game time and obviously represent his country, and unfortunately he has hurt his knee.”.

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

England always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the new half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

Recent findings suggest that will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the significant delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

In a recent development, “I make that run time and time again,” Gordon said of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

Recent findings suggest that A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

As for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

Sources indicate that “Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel remarked. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Recent findings suggest that czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL.

Recent findings suggest that england had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

Recent findings suggest that even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

According to recent reports, “I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold stated later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”.

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon said, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”.

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

It has been revealed that “If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel remarked when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against Fresh Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

“I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

Sources indicate that “But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”.

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Sources indicate that trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

“He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

Sources indicate that “He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very important player.”.

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

The Celtic Christmas advert was released on Friday containing the usual good cheer and a little festive pop at Rangers. It did, though, miss an obvious storyboard opportunity.

All I want for Christmas is my first Parkhead goal. A sad-looking, shaggy-haired striker is seen traipsing through the snowy streets of the east end of Glasgow before bumping into a dreadlocked king of kings, who gives him the gift of putting the ball in the net.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Although Henrik Larrson is not involved, Kasper Hogh does in fact feature in the latest two-minute festive promo film, which has been released in conjunction with the Celtic FC Foundation’s Christmas appeal.

It has been revealed that callum McGregor calls out “Oi, youse two!” in the direction of Hogh and Benjamin Nygren. Viljami Sinisalo is more direct: “Kasper!” Nygren turns round, and claims: “Who?”.

Recent findings suggest that it maybe doesn’t work as well when written down. Hogh – pronounced who - is clearly a good sport. However, as Martin O’Neill has stated on a number of occasions, and repeated on Friday at Lennoxtown, at some point strikers need to start scoring goals.

In a recent development, of course, Hogh thought he had finally bagged his first home goal in the hoops two weekends ago. Nygren set him up with a neat pass into the Dane’s path and seconds later the net billowed. Hogh celebrated with understandable gusto before the dismaying news that it was being ruled out for an innocuous foul in the build-up. “For him, that was a killer,” admitted O’Neill on the eve of the latest home game against St Mirren.

Industry observers note that all eyes will be on the team sheet. Will Hogh - yet to score after eight Parkhead appearances - play? Having been dropped from the Danish squad for their most recent games against Portugal and Norway, the striker was given some time off in the recent international window.

“He has been here, we have given him some time….he has had no break at all because where he came from (Norway) they were playing matches throughout (the summer),” explained O’Neill.

The manager made an extraordinary – to use one his favourite words - admission following the recent game against Kilmarnock, when Nygren wasted a spot kick. He claimed he would not have let Hogh take the penalty, which visiting keeper Nico Mantl saved, if the Dane had been on the park at the time.

Sources indicate that despite the ever more urgent need for Hogh to break his duck at home, O’Neill clearly felt the potential mental harm from failing to convert from 12 yards would have been too great a risk. The game, with Celtic winning 1-0 at the time, was also on a knife edge. A pressure penalty might not have been what Hogh needed.

It will be interesting to see what happens against St Mirren if Celtic are awarded another penalty and Hogh is available to take it. One might expect the Dane to demand to be given the ball and put this ridiculous concern to bed. Adding to the intrigue is that Nygren, who has an Achilles knock picked up on international duty with Sweden, might not play. Not that O’Neill trusts him from the spot now in any case.

The manager was not a fan of Nygren’s penalty technique against Kilmarnock. “All I will say is that if Nygren plays, which he may or may not, he won’t take it!” he stated. “All this (stuttered) walking up….why not just do an Alan Shearer and blast it into the net!? If you hit the goalkeeper, you’ll take his head off!”.

Sources indicate that non-scoring strikers is a theme just now given Oli McBurnie’s continued struggles at international level for Scotland. After just being subbed on, one wondered whether Sebastien Pocognoli might have ordered him to take the penalty against North Macedonia at Hampden Park last week. Again, with the manager’s future prospects possibly resting on the kick, maybe not. John McGinn did the necessary and Pocognoli survives, for the time being.

Hogh won’t want any handouts. He’s a centre forward who thrives on goals. He will feel capable of working it out for himself. No charity, please.

Recent findings suggest that as shown against Kilmarnock, he’s not far away. He missed one very good chance shortly after his chalked-off goal when one-on-one with Mantl. “If he had the first goal he would have taken that on another yard,” insisted O’Neill. “But that looked like a man in a real hurry to try and get his first (Celtic Park) goal.”.

Recent findings suggest that easy going and charming, there are still limits to what Hogh can endure. He wouldn’t be human if it wasn’t having an effect.

Industry observers note that “He seems philosophical about it at this minute,” O’Neill reported. “He thinks if he is working really hard for the side then he can get in….he should have taken a tip or two from Duran!”.

According to recent reports, camilo Duran is the opposite. With 13 goals in 21 appearances, he has made a flying start to his Celtic career.

According to recent reports, or maybe the aforementioned Larsson can make a visit. Like Hogh, the Swede was not an immediate hit at Parkhead.

O’Neill himself suggested Larsson could have some input - “The best thing for me to do is bring Henrik Larsson over and show him how to hit the ball into the net!” - when the discussion turned to players who initially laboured under great expectations.

Perhaps the late Trevor Francis, his old teammate, was one too? O’Neill was at Nottingham Forest when the striker arrived at the City Ground to become Britain’s first £1 million player. Talk about pressure.

Industry observers note that “He took a couple of weeks,” remembered O’Neill. “It didn’t help that he had just been signed for a million pounds and Brian Clough told him to make the tea for everyone, which he did!

Sources indicate that “First match, he made the tea for us in the dressing room! That wasn’t exactly what Trevor was expecting.” Hogh, who cost eleven times what Clough paid for Francis, has not been made to suffer such indignities - yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that an early lead in our FA Trophy tie against Chertsey Town, followed by two or three very good chances, had us thinking we might be in for a comfortable afternoon. We were on top, playing well and looking the better side.

Industry observers note that then came the moment that changed everything. A rush of blood saw Nathan Laleye bring down his man. I wasn’t convinced he was the last defender, but referee James Black saw it differently and produced a red card.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Suddenly, a game we had been controlling became a battle to survive, with around 60 minutes still to play with ten men.

Steve King reorganised, sacrificing both Paul McCallum and Darren McQueen, and the boys rolled up their sleeves. Their effort, discipline and determination were outstanding.

They held out admirably until the 85th minute, when Harry Phipps, exhausted after putting in a tremendous shift, left a leg out and conceded a penalty. Chertsey converted, and you could almost feel their energy return.

They huffed and puffed, Lewis Carey made some vital saves, and it looked as though we were heading for another penalty shootout.

Sources indicate that then came a moment of magic. A lovely move ended with Tyano Wilson slipping inside and volleying the ball into the net.

The stadium erupted. No penalties required. Just that wonderful feeling football gives you when an afternoon of tension turns into pure joy.

What a performance from a team who had spent most of the afternoon a man short. Those are the days when you learn plenty about your players, and these boys gave us every reason to be proud.

Recent findings suggest that our reward is a trip to Oxford City in the next round. Only five wins from Wembley. There is plenty of football to be played before we get carried away, but you’re allowed to dream. That’s what the cup is all about.

I just wish more people had been there to see it. You can watch the highlights, but they cannot quite recreate the feeling of being in the ground when that winner went in.

Tuesday’s free-entry game against Littlehampton brought wind, rain and, sadly, a crowd of only just over 400. We dominated the first half but squandered chance after chance and somehow went in at the break at 1-1.

Credit to Littlehampton, who battled valiantly, but our quality shone through in the second half and Borough ran out convincing 6-1 winners, with Tyano Wilson taking the man-of-the-match honours.

According to recent reports, thank you to everyone who braved the weather. We had hoped a free evening of football would tempt a few more through the gates, but we really appreciate those who came. Whether you’re a regular or it was your first visit, we hope to see you again, hopefully in kinder weather.

Tomorrow we travel to Enfield for a clash at the top of the Isthmian Premier table. A proper six-pointer, another massive test and another chance for these boys to show what they can do.

Hopefully plenty of you will be there to get behind them. If you can’t make it, Bobby’s commentary will be live so you can follow every kick.

Thank you for your support. Weeks like this remind us why we love this game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Duncan Ferguson was sent off as his unbeaten start as Glentoran manager came grinding to a halt in a 3-2 defeat at Cliftonville in the NIFL Premiership on Friday night.

The former Rangers and Everton striker was shown a straight red card and ordered from the touchline after losing his temper in the aftermath of his side falling behind at Solitude in north Belfast.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Ferguson had angrily protested against Cliftonville's opener believing there was a foul on defender Jarlath O'Rourke in the build-up and was subsequently sent to the stand by referee Ben McMaster.

Ironically, Glentoran had already equalised by the time the card was brandished with Cal Weatherup levelling the match at 1-1 just a minute after Joseph Sheridan had put the hosts in front.

The red card was Ferguson's first as a manager in his 80th appearance in the dugout but the 10th of his career overall after receiving his marching orders on nine occasions during his playing days.

Assistant manager Gary Bollan took charge for the remainder of the game as Glentoran fell behind to a Brian Healy strike in the 67th minute before equalising again through James Douglas with four minutes left.

However, Cliftonville took the three points thanks to a second goal of the night from Sheridan in the 88th minute.

Bollan handled post-match media duties as Ferguson kept his counsel.

"I think the manager got frustrated because it was a foul," Bollan said. "It changes the dynamic [the sending off], he's a leader. I've then got to step in and fill his boots and it's a major set of boots to fill.".

In the NIFL Premiership, a manager or team official given a red card receives an automatic one-match suspension for the next competitive fixture, with longer bans possible depending on the offence.

It means the former Scotland international will not be in the dugout for the Northern Ireland League Cup match against Larne at The BetMcLean Oval on Tuesday with any further punishment dependent on the content of the referee’s report.

Sources indicate that ferguson had started his Glentoran tenure with two away draws against Coleraine and Carrick before winning his first home game in charge 2-1 against Bangor last Friday. The defeat leaves Glentoran 14 points behind league leaders Linfield.

Jakirovic is boosted by the return of Algerian winger Mohamed Belloumi for Sunday's top flight meeting with Fabian Hurzeler’s second placed Brighton at the MKM Stadium.

It has been revealed that belloumi was sidelined for the1-0 loss at Arsenal just prior to the international break due to pain in his glutes and hamstring. Belloumi last featured in Hull’s draw with Ipswich Town but then started to struggle and missed training.

The 24-year-old is now in contention for a starting role against the Seagulls where he could be up against his fellow Algerian, Jaouen Hadjam, who has impressed at Brighton following his summer arrival from Swiss club Young Boys.

Meanwhile, Jakirovic is “very aware” that 13th placed Hull need to claim three points soon after recording a high number of draws.

Though still unbeaten at home in league action this season, the Tigers last won when defeating Coventry on August 29 and have had to settle for a point on five occasions since.

Brighton are faring incredibly well this term with 22 points to Hull’s 11, and Jakirovic is under no illusions as to the size of the task facing his squad and also the increasingly pressing need for a long-awaited victory.

“We have to be very aggressive because they’ll come at us, they pay very intensive football,” he remarked.

In a recent development, “A lot of high press chasing around the pitch. First balls, second balls, duels, it will be a demanding game and I hope we can respond.

“When I look back to Everton, Ipswich, Brentford, maybe we should have won two or three of those games but also we were down at Everton so at least we avoided defeat.

“That is always positive but we are very aware we lack some points and you cannot play all the time to just draw, draw, draw.

“It’s not enough, we need to take more risks on the pitch to try to win those games.”.

Albion boss Hurzeler is keen to continue their impressive start to the season but expects a tough contest at Hull.

It has been revealed that “First of all, I think they do an impressive job, “ mentioned the German. “They had a brilliant start into the Premier League.

“They are very structured, also against Arsenal I think Arsenal suffered. They didn't create a lot of massive chances, and therefore we need to be patient because we know also that Hull is really good in transition.

In a recent development, “They also have individual quality in their team. Very well-structured, very well-organised, good in transition, good in set pieces, and I think it's not an easy place to go to.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The second international break of the season is upon us, which is a good time to take stock of how things are going beyond he men’s first team.

Recent findings suggest that an ownership and management should not just be judged on one area of the club, but rather multiple different departments. The youth sector needs to be developing players in the right way, while the rising prevalence of women’s football gives added impetus to make the Femminile side as competitive as possible.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

That being said, can be hard enough keeping up with how the senior team are doing without thinking about the various other sides operating under the Milan umbrella. So, we have provided a summary of how Milan Futuro, Milan Primavera and Milan Women are doing so far in 2026-27.

Industry observers note that it was all change over the summer for the Futuro as they brought in Sergio Navarro as the head coach. The idea was to create some continuity with Ruben Amorim’s more continental style of football, and the pedigree that the Spaniard has suggested it was a positive move.

While not a necessity, the objective for the campaign will no doubt have been set as competing for promotion back to the third tier, which is the level that the project started at prior to the relegation in 2024-25.

Position: It is a case of so far, so good for Navarro’s men. They sit fourth in the standings with 23 points from 11 games, obtained through seven wins, two draws and two losses. They have scored 21 goals (third-most in the league) and allowed 15.

Importantly, the Futuro have a game in hand on the sides above them. If they win it they would go level with Chievo Verona (yes, that Chievo) and Nibbiano & Valtidone who are on 26 points. The former, however, have a 10 better goal difference.

The U23s are part of the Premier League International Cup and they got past Everton 2-1 in the first game, with matches against Stoke later this month and Tottenham in November to come, both away from home.

According to recent reports, high point: On October 18, Milan’s second team went to the current league-leaders Chievo and beat them 2-1, with Bonomi scoring a late winner. That was an early marker of what this team are capable of. A special mention must go to the Premier League Cup win at Goodison Park against Everton, too.

Recent findings suggest that low point: That aforementioned win in Verona came in the round after Milan had lost 2-1 at home to Rovato Vertovese. They are a side that have only won twice all season and at the moment occupy the relegation spots, so it was a big blow before a big response.

Key players: There have been multiple players that have stood out. Levin Asanji has scored four goals in the league, as has Lorenzo Ossolo. Fabio Pandolfi has been playing a deeper midfield role and looks to have quality well beyond his 18 years of age, with three goals to his name.

Silvano Vos is having a resurgence, while the likes of Emanuele Sala, Mattia Cappelletti, Alessandro Bonomi and Emanuele Borsani have all started every single game, aiding their development under the upcoming coach. El Hadji Malick Cisse – a January arrival – is also turning a lot of heads.

For a bit more deeper reading on the tactical approach used by Milan Futuro under Navarro, we suggest reading the analysis we put out over the international break.

In a recent development, the 2025-26 season was a mixed one for the Primavera side, as their record of 11 wins and 11 defeats in 38 games shows perfectly. They finished 11th, nine points off the relegation play-offs but 10 points off the Scudetto play-offs, though a lot of the younger talents had been again accelerated into the Futuro side.

It has been revealed that giovanni Renna remained at the helm going into the upcoming campaign, the coach that has been promoted up the ranks and thus knows a lot of the players. The hope was that continuity would yield better results, and so far it has.

Position: At the time of writing, the U20 side are sixth in the Primavera 1 league, which puts them in a final play-off spot. They have won five of their first 10 games but they have also lost four, so they remain a bit of a rollercoaster ride of inconsistency.

Sources indicate that looking upwards, Parma are right now top on 21 points, but the Rossoneri are within striking distance of Inter, who are in second on 19 points. However, Renna’s side are also a bad round away from being in the bottom half too.

It has been revealed that milan Primavera progressed in the Coppa Italia Primavera at the end of October, beating Catanzaro 2-1 thanks to a late winner from Dotta. Como are the opponents in the next round.

High point: It’s hard to look past the last two rounds in truth. The Primavera seem to have really clicked, scoring 10 goals in the last 180 minutes of action, beating Monza 5-0 away from home and then AlbinoLeffe 5-1 at home.

An honourable mention must go to the 2-0 win over Juventus in September, given they are in a similar position with also having a B-team (Juve Next Gen), so they will continue to serve as a useful point of comparison.

It has been revealed that low point: Back on October 10, the young Diavoli lost 2-0 against Atalanta which was their third league defeat in a row. There was talk of crisis mode as the slide down the table continued, and against an Atalanta side that are now third-bottom of the league. Thankfully, they turned it around swiftly.

In a recent development, key players: A bit like with the Futuro, the goals have been shared around the Milan Primavera squad. Mattia Zaramella has emerged recently as a star with four goals, as has Max Anastasio who arrived from Bologna and has the same amount.

Industry observers note that then, Andrea Cullotta (a centre-back), Vincent Ibrahimovic (a midfielder) and Edoardo Tartaglia (a full-back) all have two goals. Renna has called upon the same core group of players largely. Matteo Geroli, Francesco Domnitei, Cullotta, Zaramella, Tartaglia, Anastasio and Yanis Massaouadi have all appeared in every round.

It has been revealed that last season was not one that Milan Women will want to shout about, given that they finished sixth in the table and seven points off the play-off spots in the end. They won just nine of 22 games, placing them below even Fiorentina and Lazio, plus Juventus, city rivals Inter and eventual champions Roma.

However, like with the Primavera, consistency was the name of the game. So, Suzanne Bakker remained as the head coach, and there wasn’t as much player turnover as in some recent years.

Position: There have only been seven rounds so far in Serie A Femminile, but the Rossonere have got off to a stuttering start. They have just seven points from their opening seven games, which puts them in eighth place in the table. They have scored 11 goals but let in a joint-league-high 16.

In a recent development, looking upwards, Roma lead the way with 21 points having won every game. Inter are second on 16 points – so nine more than Milan – while Juventus occupy the final play-off spot on 12. Over their shoulders, Sassuolo are in bottom (the only relegation spot), with three points.

In the Women’s Cup, Milan drew 1-1 with Como, beat Como 1907 (affiliated with the men’s team presently in Serie A, the others are a stand-alone club) 2-1, and then lost 1-0 to Juventus to end their campaign.

High point: This one is quite an easy pick, and it has to be the 2-1 victory over Juventus last month. Thea Kyvåg and Monica Renzotti overturned Lenzini’s opener, which had come with just under a quarter of an hour left on the clock, engineering a late comeback that sparked jubilant scenes.

It has been revealed that low point: The tone for what has been a disappointing campaign so far for Bakker’s ladies was set in round one, when they were beaten 4-1 by Como 1907. Then, losing 1-0 away at Como was another dark day, given they have only won twice.

On November 7, the 3-0 derby defeat to Inter – which included a red card for Milan – served only to highlight the significant gulf between the two teams at the moment.

Key players: Christy Grimshaw remains the shining light for Milan Women, with three goals and an assist to her name. The scoring charts then see Sara Stokic on three goals, with Sara Fornes, Park Soojeong and Monica Renzotti all netting twice.

It has been revealed that grimshaw is one of three players to start every game so far under Bakker, with the others being defenders Angelica Soffia and Nerea Nevado. Sandra Estevez has emerged as the number one between the sticks too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:25 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 08:02 EST, 17 November 2026.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers manager due to ill health.

The 62-year-old, who previously had to walk away from his job at Birmingham City in 2024 due to a battle with bowel cancer, leaves Blackburn with immediate effect.

The Championship side announced his departure with a statement from Mowbray. It read: 'Unfortunately, due to health challenges, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

Recent findings suggest that 'I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

'Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

According to recent reports, 'To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Tony Mowbray has stepped down from his role as Blackburn Rovers boss due to ill health.

'I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail (Pasha, chief operating officer) for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

Recent findings suggest that 'I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.'.

Mowbray leaves with Blackburn 13th in the Championship. He took over at the club in June this year having spent two years out of the game following his health complications at Birmingham City.

According to recent reports, the veteran manager suddenly stepped down as manager of Birmingham in February 2024 after undergoing surgery for bowel cancer. He had 15cm of his bowel removed during his treatment.

He took a temporary leave of absence after eight games in charge, before officially resigning from the role in May.

Mowbray, who has managed a host of English clubs, opened up publicly about his struggles, telling the Times that his children had feared the worst.

According to recent reports, 'I had the conversation with my family and you could see they were frightened,' he noted. 'Was I frightened? My only thoughts were for my family, my three children and my wife and making sure they were OK.

Recent findings suggest that 'I had to put everything in order and I tried to. My wife saw our banking app for the first time in her life. It's little things like that. She understood. This was serious stuff. I felt she needed to know where we had our money, whether it was ISAs or pensions and what was in the bank.'.

In a recent development, speaking on his diagnosis, which came after he collapsed when trying to answer the door, he added: 'My wife put me in the car and drove me back to hospital and they wanted to know why I was collapsing and in the condition I was,' he indicates. 'They rehydrated me and put me on a drip overnight.

'I remember sitting there in bed and my kids' eyes were watering up. They were scared I wasn't going to live. How old were they? They were 15, 17 and 19. I could see the fear in their eyes.'.

Mowbray's comeback story when he was made Blackburn boss in the summer was one of the feel-good moments of the offseason. It has not been disclosed what his current health issue is.

Mowbray leaves Blackburn with the team in 13th place in the Championship table.

Blackburn Rovers owner Balaji Rao added his own statement, writing: 'Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

'Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

According to recent reports, 'Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.'.

Chief Executive Officer Steve Curwood noted: 'Tony’s passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he shows for players, staff and those around him that mean so much.

'Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.

'On behalf of everyone at Blackburn Rovers, I would like to send Tony and his family our very best wishes during this time.'.

Brighton have confirmed Pascal Gross has agreed a latest contract until June 2028.

The Germany international, who made 261 appearances during his first spell with Albion, rejoined the club in January after 18 months in the Bundesliga with Borussia Dortmund.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The 35-year-old is poised to make his 300th Albion appearance in Sunday's Premier League match against Hull City.

Head coach Fabian Hurzeler noted: "We are really pleased that Pascal has signed a new contract.

"We can talk about his many qualities on the pitch - his goals, assists and football intelligence - but he is also a great leader within the group.

"He connects different generations and different nationalities in our squad. He's so valuable because he helps everyone understand what it takes to be successful.".

Pascal joined Albion from Ingolstadt in 2017 and played a key role in establishing the club in the Premier League, becoming one of its most influential players during his first seven seasons.

The midfielder helped Albion secure its highest-ever league finishes and qualification for the Europa League in 2023 and the Conference League last season.

He has been involved in 87 Premier League goals, scoring 35 times and providing 52 assists, the joint-highest total of goal involvements by a German player in the competition's history.

His performances for Albion earned him a first senior Germany call-up in 2023. He has won 19 caps and featured at this summer's FIFA World Cup.

Hurzeler, speaking ahead of Brighton’s trip to Hull, said: “He connects different generations, and we have different generations in our team.

“He connects different nationalities, and we have a lot of different nationalities in our team. He's very adaptive to every personality, and he finds access to every person.

“I think that's something we shouldn't underestimate, and therefore he's so valuable because he gives everyone an understanding of what it needs to be successful.

“No matter if you are 19, 20 years old, no matter if you are 27 or 32, and no matter where you come from, it's all about our standards.

“He's a great standard driver, culture driver, together with Jason (Steele), together with Lewis (Dunk). They are very helpful in driving these things, and therefore I think that's his biggest impact.

“Of course, we can speak about all his goals and assists and football understanding, but being that connector beside the pitch is very valuable.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 20 Nov 2026 12:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 20:11.

Arsenal reportedly remain interested in signing Brentford attacker Kevin Schade during the January transfer window.

Bolstering the left-wing position, along with bringing in a new striker, are priorities for Mikel Arteta, and several players have been linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium in recent weeks.

Schade joined the Bees in January 2023 and has since made 118 appearances for the club, scoring 25 goals.

The German attacker has made 10 Premier League appearances this season, starting nine of them, and has scored three goals so far.

According to TEAMTalk, Arsenal view Schade as a strong candidate to add depth and competition across their forward line.

Schade is primarily a left-sided forward but possesses the versatility to operate across the frontline, a quality that appeals to Arteta.

The winger is regarded as a realistic and proven Premier League option for the Gunners, given his ability to make an immediate impact.

While Arsenal's interest is genuine, any potential move would depend on Brentford's valuation and how Schade's contract negotiations with the club progress.

Schade has entered the final two years of his Brentford contract, and the club have reportedly opened talks with the player over a fresh deal.

The Bees are noted to be keen to offer him a latest long-term contract on improved terms, underlining his growing importance in Keith Andrews's squad.

The Gunners could face competition from Premier League rivals Liverpool, who have reportedly emerged as serious contenders in the race for Schade.

Arsenal are also stated to be keeping tabs on RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa, although they would need to pay a substantial transfer fee to prise him away from the German club.

#49242. Breaking: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 157m • 📚 Deep Dive (31496 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 157 min read (31496 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~157 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as a primary port of pathogen entry, the intestinal mucosa has developed a sophisticated set of defences to ward off infections.
  • The human intestine coordinates nutrient absorption with immune surveillance of luminal commensal and pathogenic microorganisms2.
  • It has been revealed that this context-dependent crosstalk is executed through a multi-barrier system comprising a patterned epithelium, a protective mucus layer and specialized tissue-resident immune cells5.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as a primary port of pathogen entry, the intestinal mucosa has developed a sophisticated set of defences to ward off infections. Investigating the human-specific intestinal barrier responses to pathogens is limited by the lack of models integrating the necessary architectural complexity with an autologous immune compartment1. Here we developed engineered barrier models of the human small intestine and colon combining a multilineage epithelium, mucus layer, accessible microbial compartment and autologous tissue-resident immune cells. These tissues recapitulate morphological and functional properties that are region specific and compare with those of the native organ. We use the model to characterize the human epithelial response to Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium at the single-cell level, uncovering the distinct gene regulatory networks that underpin luminal versus intracellular pathogen presence. Invaded epithelial cells initiate an IL-18 signalling axis that triggers cytotoxic T cell activation, resulting in epithelial shedding and barrier disruption. Overall, this work allows for the modular integration of epithelial, microbial and immune compartments, providing a versatile system for studying human intestinal physiology and pathologies.

The human intestine coordinates nutrient absorption with immune surveillance of luminal commensal and pathogenic microorganisms2. Controlled host–microbe interactions shape diverse aspects of human biology, including epithelial maturation and systemic immunity while maintaining a protective barrier against infection3. Conversely, dysregulated interactions contribute to pathologies such as inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer4.

It has been revealed that this context-dependent crosstalk is executed through a multi-barrier system comprising a patterned epithelium, a protective mucus layer and specialized tissue-resident immune cells5. Integration of these three components is required to meaningfully capture intestine–microbe interactions in a human-relevant setting1.

Intestinal stem cell (ISC)-derived organoids provide key inroads into human epithelial biology6. However, intestinal organoids face limitations recapitulating intestinal physiology, owing to an inaccessible lumen, culture heterogeneity, lack of biomimetic morphology and absence of non-epithelial lineages7,8. Although bioengineered 3D extracellular matrix (ECM) scaffolds have helped to overcome some of these challenges by establishing crypt–villus architecture and apical–basal access9, physiological integration of epithelial, tissue-resident immune and microbial compartments remains a major challenge1,10.

Here we established engineered immunocompetent human intestinal models composed of autologous tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells and small intestinal or colonic ISC-derived epithelia amenable to luminal manipulation. Multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) characterization of these barriers reveal region-specific spatial niches, mucus layer formation and immune–epithelium interactions. Applying this system to Salmonella Typhimurium (S.Tm), we provide a single-cell multiomic view of the epithelial responses to luminal and intracellular infection. Finally, we modelled the pathogen–epithelial–immune axis, demonstrating that TRM cells respond to S.Tm invasion by cytokine release and concomitant epithelial damage, which may facilitate pathogen clearance and infection resolution.

It has been revealed that to model the human intestinal epithelium, we developed a fluidic device and microstamping technology to impart crypt-mimicking topography on an embedded ECM-like hydrogel (Extended Data Fig. 1a). Human intestinal organoids were seeded into the top reservoir of the device, where they formed a tight, polarized barrier comprising crypt units sustained by basal nutrition (Fig. 1a–d and Extended Data Fig. 1b–e).

Regions shown: the duodenum, ileum and colon (a,d,e,g–l), ileum (b) and duodenum (c,f).

It has been revealed that to characterize the morphology, cellular composition and patterning of the epithelium, we developed a 3D-printed ‘histomold’ for simultaneous embedding and perpendicular sectioning of up to 50 engineered epithelia (Extended Data Fig. 1f). Haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and mIF staining demonstrated histological and cell-type patterning similarity to donor-matched primary tissue (Fig. 1e and Extended Data Figs. 1g and 2a–c). In addition, a duodenal dual reporter line stably labelling chromatin (H2BC4–mTurquoise2) and LGR5+ stem cells (LGR5–IRES-NLS-mScarlet3) confirmed LGR5 ISC localization to the crypt bottom (Fig. 1f). By day 10, the thick epithelium contained proliferative SOX9+ and Ki67+ cells primarily confined to the crypt, whereas mature enterocytes (APOA4+ in the duodenum, and FABP6+ in the ileum) and colonocytes (CA1+) were enriched within inter-crypt regions (Fig. 1g and Extended Data Fig. 3a–f), with αDEF5+ Paneth cells detected in some small intestinal crypts (Extended Data Fig. 3g). EdU pulse-chase labelling revealed that cycling cells, initially localized in the crypt base, progressively migrated towards the apical surface over 4 days, similar to homeostatic turnover in vivo11 (Extended Data Fig. 3h and Supplementary Video 1). These data confirm that imposing in vivo-inspired geometries on human intestinal organoids drives reproducible cell-type regionalization and migration akin to the intestinal crypt–villus axis9.

Recent findings suggest that multiplexed scRNA-seq demonstrated region-specific stem, absorptive and secretory lineages across seven donors at day 10 (Fig. 1h–j, Extended Data Fig. 4a,b and Supplementary Tables 1 and 2). Cell-type composition was similar to primary tissue counterparts and proportions were consistent across donors, highlighting the fidelity and robustness of the system (Fig. 1k and Extended Data Fig. 4c). Gene Ontology analysis of enterocyte and colonocyte marker genes revealed enrichment of distinct physiological programs concordant with the primary intestinal regions12,13 (Extended Data Fig. 4d and Supplementary Tables 3 and 4). Proximal small intestinal enterocytes demonstrated higher expression of genes involving lipid, xenobiotic and iron metabolism (Fig. 1l and Extended Data Fig. 4d). Pseudotemporal ordering of the duodenal stem-to-enterocyte trajectory confirmed enterocyte maturation levels, approaching the AQP10+ expression observed at the villus tip in vivo14 (Extended Data Fig. 4e). Distal small intestinal enterocytes expressed bile acid and vitamin B12 transport genes, whereas colonocytes were enriched in cell–cell interactions and ion transport13,15 (Fig. 1l and Extended Data Fig. 4d). We confirmed differential protein expression of the transporters SLC5A1, SLC10A2 and SLC26A2 between the regions (Fig. 1l and Extended Data Fig. 4f). Among secretory lineages, enteroendocrine cells and goblet cells were differentially abundant, with substantial heterogeneity in enteroendocrine cells (CHGA+) including EC (TPH1+), MX (GHRL+ and MLN+), D (SST+), K (GIP+), I (CCK+) and L (GCG+ and PYY+) subpopulations that match tissue distribution16 (Extended Data Figs. 2 and 4g–j).

Collectively, these data show that the engineered epithelium retains region-specific cell composition, spatial organization and gene expression, providing inroads to explore nutrient, xenobiotic and host–microbe processes in a human context.

The mucus, a layered network of mucins, cellular material, antimicrobials and structural factors, provides an interactive barrier between the microbiome and intestinal epithelium. Characterizing the properties and functional role of the mucus at the host–microbe interface remains largely under-explored in vitro. To facilitate rapid accumulation of mucus, we reduced the apical volume over the course of approximately 4 days, which resulted in a fibrous mucus network covering the epithelium (Fig. 2a,b and Extended Data Fig. 5a,b). Shed cells were present throughout the mucus layer, where they contribute to viscosity17 and can exert an antimicrobial role18 (Extended Data Fig. 5b,c). Longitudinal sections revealed an irregular mucus profile, with higher colonic thickness and crypt plumes similar to observations in primary tissue19 (Fig. 2c–e and Extended Data Fig. 5d–g). AlcianBlue–Periodic Acid–Schiff (PAS) co-staining highlighted regional differences in secretion and glycosylation, with higher ratios of acidic, negatively charged groups towards colon (Fig. 2f and Extended Data Fig. 5h,i). These patterns were comparable with the primary tissue and may be influenced by relative levels of fucose, sialic acid and sulfate groups20. Proteomic analysis of the colonic luminal content identified the core mucus layer proteins21 (MUC2, FCGBP, TFF3, AGR2, CLCA1, ZG16 and MUC5B) as major constituents, alongside additional mucins, antimicrobials and lectin-binding proteins (Fig. 2g, Extended Data Fig. 5j and Supplementary Table 5). Using the scRNA-seq data, we identified seven non-proliferative (MKI67−) goblet cell clusters (C0–C6) representing regional diversity and differentiation state (Fig. 2h, Extended Data Fig. 5k and Supplementary Table 3). Colonic goblet cells (C1) were enriched in intracellular vesicle transport, protein glycosylation and aerobic respiration, suggesting a higher secretion machinery consistent with thickness measurements (Extended Data Fig. 5l and Supplementary Table 4).

Next, we benchmarked the expression of membrane-bound mucins, key glycocalyx components that fortify the epithelium but remain difficult to recapitulate in vitro22. We observed a strong cell-type and region-specific gene expression comparable with the reference tissue (Fig. 2i). MUC6 and MUC5AC, which encode stomach mucins that are often expressed under pathological and metaplastic conditions23,24, were nearly absent. MUC12 and MUC17 staining in the engineered epithelium and tissue counterparts confirmed the specificity and maturation of the glycocalyx, revealing in vivo-like levels by day 12 of culture (Fig. 2j,k and Extended Data Fig. 5m). Finally, we functionally assessed the mucus upon colonization with the commensals Enterococcus faecium or Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus, which proliferated without compromising epithelial integrity (Fig. 2l and Extended Data Fig. 5n). Together, these results indicate that the platform can accumulate a complex mucus layer with in vivo-like and region-specific properties, opening new avenues for the study of human mucus and host–microbe interactions.

Sources indicate that unlike commensal microbiota, the foodborne pathogen S.Tm exploits motility and adhesion mechanisms to penetrate the mucus25, triggering an invasion-dependent inflammatory response that facilitates pathogen colonization26. Although extensive research has characterized the fundamental mechanisms underlying S.Tm infection, the exact epithelial responses and the resulting epithelial–immune signalling remain unresolved at the human level and at single-cell resolution.

Industry observers note that motivated by the higher mucus level and its potential role against pathogenic bacteria, we infected colonic epithelium with S.Tm 14028 in conditions with varying densities of mucus. At 18 h post-start of the infection (hpi), S.Tm triggered strong damage in conditions with less mucus (Mucuslo), whereas the epithelium remained largely unaffected in the presence of dense mucus (Mucushi; Fig. 3a–d and Extended Data Fig. 6a–d). Furthermore, the denser mucus led to a decrease in microbial burden, cell invasion and cytokine release, while preserving barrier integrity (Extended Data Fig. 6e–g). These protective effects were coupled with cell shedding, which predominantly localized at crypt openings, presumably impeding bacterial colonization (Extended Data Fig. 6h).
